issues.description: The problem statement and both Dockerfiles reference and attempt to COPY a start.sh script into the image and make it executable, but no start.sh file exists in the template or solution repository. This is a structural inconsistency: the Docker build (as described in the instructions and implemented in the Dockerfiles) depends on a file that is not present in the repository, which will prevent students from successfully building the Docker image as instructed and cause confusion about what start.sh should contain.
issues.suggestedFix:
Include a start.sh script in the repository root (or update the Dockerfiles). The start.sh should run the application, e.g.:

#!/bin/sh
java -jar /app/app.jar

and be committed to the repository with executable permissions. Alternatively, modify the Dockerfile to directly run the jar (e.g. use CMD ["java","-jar","/app/app.jar"]) and remove the COPY/CHMOD references to start.sh. Ensure the problem statement and Dockerfile instructions match the chosen approach.
